content.comment_body: Hello, I have two analog input [product_name] modules connected to a [product_name] controller. It's powered with 24V DC. How do I reference these analog inputs in the [product_name] software? Analog inputs on the main module are usually labeled as i1, i2, i7, and i8. I'm not planning to use these and have disabled them in the 'select hardware' section of the software. Will the software automatically assign any analog inputs I use to those of the expansion modules? Thank you.

If your main module has 4 analog inputs, 2 out of a possible 8 analog inputs are reserved by default. You can adjust this in the settings page of [product_name] software: File > Properties > Offline Settings > I/O settings Here, you can specify in pairs how many of the 8 possible analog inputs are allocated to the main module. If 0 analog inputs are assigned to the main module: The first expansion module gets AI1 and AI2. If 2 analog inputs are assigned to the main module: Then AI1 (I7) and AI2 (I8) go to the main module, and AI3 and AI4 go to the first expansion module. If 4 analog inputs are assigned to the main module: Then AI1 (I7), AI2 (I8), AI3 (I1), and AI4 (I2) are for the main module, and AI5 and AI6 are for the first expansion module.
Hello, Thank you for your reply. Your explanation matches what I was thinking.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are seeking clarity on how analogue inputs from expansion modules are referenced within [product_name] software, especially when built-in analogue inputs on the main module are deactivated. There is some uncertainty about how inputs are assigned and configured in the software, and answers emphasize that configuration is done through I/O settings, with input mapping dependent on user selection.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to assign analog input references to expansion modules when main module inputs are turned off, and they want straightforward options for analog input assignment.
